name: National Gallery of Victoria
notes: National Gallery of Victoria, St Kilda Road (Roy Grounds, 1968): a long, nearly windowless two-storey block of grey bluestone, about 150 m by 74 m, set in a moat; the tall round-headed entrance arch on St Kilda Road with the Water Wall behind it; three internal courtyards; the Great Hall at the back under Leonard French's stained-glass ceiling; the sculpture garden behind. Footprint, the moat's line and the road from the ground file (the real building is turned a few degrees off north; the model is square to it). Written from general knowledge. Guessed: courtyard sizes and positions, the height (about 18 m), the roof lanterns. Bluestone drawn in the grey 'concrete' material. No photographs were available (Wikimedia still blocked). Refined 27 Sep 2026 without photographs: the roof is a gravel field inside a stone parapet rather than a pale slab; St Kilda Road's elms are one fuller row with the axis to the arch kept clear; the two garden courts are glazed at ground level, where the galleries look into them after the 2003 Bellini refurbishment. Still guessed: the roof's skylights and the courts' exact glazing.
